Sedjem 0.3.3 updates the engines that run Cohere Transcribe Arabic and the speaker models, shows where new
versions are announced, and is the first release whose builds download only pinned and checked files.

## Download

- Windows 10 and 11: `Sedjem-0.3.3-setup.exe` installs for your user, without admin rights. It isn't
  signed yet, so SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher: choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
  Installing over 0.3.2 keeps your transcriptions, keys and models.
- Linux (x64): unpack `Sedjem-0.3.3-linux-x64.tar.gz` and run `Sedjem/Sedjem`.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of both.

0.3.2 can update itself: *Settings → Updates*, then *Update now*.

## Engines

- transcribe.cpp, which runs Cohere Transcribe Arabic on your computer, goes from 0.2.3 to 0.4.1. On a
  26-minute Egyptian Arabic–English meeting, on Intel graphics, Sedjem gave the same lines, speakers and start
  times as with 0.2.3, and the same text in 160 of the 161 lines, about 5% faster. The other line is a long
  hesitation: 0.2.3 turned it into a runaway string of letters, and 0.4.1 writes one letter.
- sherpa-onnx, which runs the speaker models TitaNet and 3D-Speaker CAM++, goes from 1.13.8 to 2.0.1.
- yt-dlp, which reads YouTube links, goes to 2026.10.26, and NumPy to 2.5.4.

## Follow new versions

- *Settings → About* links the project's
  [Discussions](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/sedjem/discussions). Each stable version is announced
  there from now on, starting with this one, and questions and ideas are welcome too.
- On GitHub, *Watch → Custom → Releases* sends an email for each release, the nightly previews included.

## Built from pinned downloads

- Everything the builds download is pinned: every Python package comes from a lock with the SHA-256 of its files,
  every GitHub action is pinned to a commit, and each program a build downloads is checked against its SHA-256
  before it runs. The build machine's own Python and Inno Setup, which GitHub provides, are the exceptions.
- Every change is checked by CodeQL, and a change may not add a finding that the main line doesn't have. The
  OpenSSF Scorecard rates the project's practices every week.

## The website and the README

- The [website](https://mohammedel-sayedahmed.github.io/sedjem/) shows the benchmarks in one place, and its
  anonymous counts note the tag of a shared link, such as `?src=linkedin`, only when it is on a short list. The
  [privacy policy](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/sedjem/blob/main/docs/privacy.md#the-website) has the
  list.
- The README is rewritten, with the download first and sharper pictures of the app.

## Known limits

- The installer is unsigned, and macOS isn't built.
- winget doesn't have Sedjem yet; `winget install MohammedElsayedAhmed.Sedjem` will work once winget has accepted
  the package.
- Running on another computer has been tried with two copies of Sedjem on one computer, not yet between two
  computers on many networks. The first time it is turned on, Windows asks whether to let Sedjem through its
  firewall: allow it on private networks only.
- On Linux, *Update now* unpacks the new build next to the old one rather than replacing it.
- Nemotron-3-Diarization hears at most 8 speakers.

Every commit: [v0.3.2...v0.3.3](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/sedjem/compare/v0.3.2...v0.3.3).
